newsitem.title: USA: Forbes opposes anticipated interest rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Forbes opposes anticipated interest rate hike.

text.p: An expected increase in short-term interest rates by Federal Reserve policy makers is premature and unnecessary, former presidential candidate and magazine publisher Steve Forbes said on Monday.

Recent comments by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan have convinced many experts that the Federal Open Market Committee will choose to raise rates at its meeting on Tuesday to try to slow the economy and head off inflation.
"That's not necessary. The economy's not overheating," Forbes said. "Prosperity does not cause inflation, excessive credit does."
Forbes said that because Greenspan is worried about the stock market "he has it within his power to make it a self-fulfilling prophecy by creating conditions for stocks to take a hit."
"Overall, most stocks are down this year from where they began the year, if you look at the whole universe. And that's not to me a good sign," Forbes told a Rotary International luncheon.
The magazine publisher also urged Congress to pass a cut in the capital gains tax this year.
Forbes said he has formed an organisation Americans for Hope, Growth and Opportunity that will use radio advertising to promote a flat tax proposal.
